thread:
Aisha (oncall): :rotating_light: euc1 alerts: surge in 504/502 from inference ELB and a spike in NAT gateway connection failures. Seeing ~40% of serving requests fail. Rooting this here.
Ben (sre): Confirming. ELB target health shows healthy but TCP resets from instances. NAT metrics show ephemeral port exhaustion on the SNAT table for the private subnets. High ephemeral port reuse & SNAT entries are being flushed.
Carlos (infra): What triggered the SNAT flush? Any recent config rollouts or autoscaling churn?
Aisha (oncall): No config rollouts in the last hour in euc1. Autoscaling activity normal. NAT gateway CloudWatch logs show a burst of simultaneous connections from ML-serving tasks, long-lived connections to model storage + many short model pull requests.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-4623 | Region: eu-central-1 | Sev: sev2 | Services: ELB, EC2, NAT Gateway | Pager: Aisha
Dana (prod): We have customer reports of inference timeouts and degraded quality for active production jobs. Major customers in EU are impacted. ETA on mitigation?
Ben (sre): Short-term mitigation: reduce ephemeral port reuse by forcing connection churn down and rotate outbound path. Plan: 1) Create temporary NAT gateway in a different AZ and add route table rule for a subset of subnets. 2) Add connection timeout tweak on docker hosts to shorten TIME_WAIT. 3) Apply per-service egress rate limiting to model pullers.
Carlos (infra): I'm provisioning a new NAT in eu-central-1c and will attach to the private route table for the ML-serving subnets. Pushing now.
Aisha (oncall): Noted. Start traffic cutover for 10% of serving traffic to the new NAT once it's ready.
Ben (sre): Also enabling ELB slow-start=60s and increase idle timeout to 120s to reduce connection churn.
Carlos (infra): NAT in 1c is up. Route table updated for subnet-ml-02 to use new NAT (temporary). Verifying connectivity.
Aisha (oncall): @Dana can you confirm whether customer-facing jobs on subnet-ml-02 improved?
Dana (prod): Early signs: reduced 502s for that subset, customers on that subset show retry success. Still seeing failures on other subnets.
Ben (sre): Good. Rolling out same route table change for subnet-ml-01 and subnet-ml-03, staggered with 2m between to avoid overload.
incident-bot: ACTION: route-change applied to subnet-ml-02 by Carlos at 2625009988
Aisha (oncall): After second cutover, backend 5xx rate dropped from 42% -> 8% overall. Still seeing elevated latency for some requests. Where are we on SNAT table entries?
Carlos (infra): SNAT table size dropped after cutovers. Ephemeral port exhaustion relieved on the switched subnets. Remaining pressure from model pullers that create many short-lived outbound connections. Suggest long-term fix: reuse HTTP connection pools in model fetcher, or proxy fetches through an internal gateway.
Ben (sre): For immediate further relief, I've changed host tcp_tw_reuse and tcp_tw_recycle flags temporarily and lowered conntrack timeout to 30s on nodes running model pullers. Pushing now via runbook.
Aisha (oncall): Applying changes. Please monitor for any regression.
incident-bot: RUNBOOK STEP: modify sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1 ; net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=30
Carlos (infra): Sysctl applied to 80% of nodes. Conntrack table size trending down.
Dana (prod): Customer impact update: 4 enterprise accounts reported retries during the spike; our synthetic checks show 99.1% success over last 5m (improved). We're still below SLO for a few customers.
Ben (sre): Preparing a canary config for the model puller to enable connection pooling (keep-alive) on a small percentage (5%) of instances. If healthy, we'll roll more broadly.
Aisha (oncall): Go ahead, Carlos will coordinate canary.
Carlos (infra): Canary deployed to ml-puller-canary-1. Metrics: connection count per process fell 70% for the canary.
incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: ELB 5xx rate = 7.9% -> 2.1% after canary and host changes
Dana (prod): We're seeing customer jobs recover with successful retries. Proactive comms ready? I can draft a message noting a regional network egress issue affecting inference in eu-central-1 that we mitigated; we'll follow up with a postmortem.
Aisha (oncall): Yes draft and include mitigations and temporary workarounds. Tag enterprise CSMs.
Ben (sre): Next steps for closure: 1) Revert transient tcp flags to defaults per post-incident change plan. 2) Schedule a change to introduce an internal egress proxy or increase NAT capacity. 3) Add a Route53 health-check and auto-shift policy for ELB when NAT pressure is detected.
Carlos (infra): I'll open infra ticket to provision additional NAT capacity and design the egress-proxy. Also will add CloudWatch Alarm for SNAT entries > 80%.
Aisha (oncall): Handoff to night oncall: Ben, please summarize: cause = SNAT ephemeral port exhaustion due to model puller connection churn causing NAT table flushes and outbound conn failures -> ELB 5xx for inference. Mitigation = temporary NAT in different AZ + sysctl conntrack timeouts + connection pooling canary. Impact = degraded inference for EU customers (~40% failure at peak), now reduced to <1% with mitigations. Follow-ups = egress proxy, increase NAT capacity, improved monitoring and runbooks.
Ben (sre): I'll add that to the incident ticket and notify pagerduty to assign night oncall. Adding timeline and artifacts.
Aisha (oncall): Thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated. I'll keep channel open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
pagerduty: PAGED: Ben (night-oncall) at 2625013400 for handoff
Ben (sre): Acknowledged, taking handoff. Will coordinate postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: STATUS=mitigated | SEVERITY=se v2 -> sev3 | MITIGATION_TIME=2625012000
Dana (prod): Draft comms posted to #customer-ops, will route to CSMs and affected accounts.
Aisha (oncall): Closing thread; please add any additional observations.
